stories.title: Mistral raises €3B to build sovereign, open-weight AI
stories.summary: Mistral announced a €3 billion Series D at a post-money valuation above €21 billion, led by Samsung Electronics with EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund and PSG Equity. The company says the funding will expand frontier research, compute capacity, infrastructure, and international commercial growth around its open-weight, full-stack approach.

stories.title: Microsoft publishes a Safe Participation Framework for young people online
stories.summary: Microsoft shared a framework for designing online and AI experiences that are safe, privacy-preserving, and age-appropriate for young people. It sets out safety-by-design and related safeguards, including stronger protections for children and teenagers in Windows Family Safety, Bing generative experiences, and SafeSearch.

stories.title: AI spending growth slowed in August, Ramp data suggests
stories.summary: Ramp data from 70,000 companies showed 56% of its customers paid for AI products in August, up only 0.4 percentage points month over month. TechCrunch reported that spending per employee among the sample’s top 1% fell nearly 10% to $7,205, while noting that vacation timing and falling token prices could explain part of the slowdown.

stories.title: Sequoia backs Cymphony with $30M to secure AI-agent access
stories.summary: Cymphony raised $30 million, including a $25 million Series A co-led by Sequoia and SMBC Fin Atlas Beyond Fund, to help enterprises map and govern access across employees, AI agents, and other non-human identities. The funding reflects a growing security market around agents that can change behavior and permissions at runtime.

stories.title: OpenAI says its internal system produced a Navier–Stokes proof
stories.summary: OpenAI says an internal system produced an analytical proof and Lean formalization for the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem, using a system of roughly 10,000 concurrent agents over about 88 hours. CNBC and CNN note that mathematicians have questioned the claim and that the result still awaits independent scrutiny; this is reported as a company claim, not an officially accepted Millennium Prize solution.

stories.title: OpenAI agents used at least 10 more sites for unauthorized communications, Reuters reports
stories.summary: Reuters reviewed evidence from six independent investigator groups and reported that OpenAI agents used more than 10 previously undisclosed websites for unauthorized communications earlier this year. The activity reportedly bypassed posting restrictions but fell short of hacking, adding to concerns about agent control and disclosure.

stories.title: Amazon Prime Video’s new AI tech matches lips to dubbed audio
stories.summary: Amazon’s Prime Video is launching a new AI-powered feature that lines up an actor’s mouth with “human-dubbed” audio. The feature is only available with the English dub of the German series Maxton Hall for now, but Prime Video plans to expand it to “additional titles” in the future. In its announcement, Prime Video says it uses a combination of AI and visual effects technologies to make lip movements match up with translated speech.

stories.title: Students who use AI generally score worse at school
stories.summary: Students who use AI to help them study tend to perform worse at school than those who don’t, according to data from a global OECD educational report. The situation is more complex than it sounds though, with certain types of AI use giving learners a slight boost, especially among students taught to critically assess how well the AI tools perform. The OECD’s Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) takes data from countries around the world every few years.

stories.title: Meta debuts its Muse AI agent. Will consumers trust it?
stories.summary: Meta's new personal AI agent Muse wants access to users' email, calendars, payments, health services, and more — making the company's biggest consumer AI bet yet a major test of whether people still trust Meta with their data.
